pass_a_gloss: Give place through the eagerness for martyrdom to the Spirit of your Father speaking to those handed over through godliness; if you see yourselves hated and abominable and thought to be impious, then take up: 'through this the world hates you', 'because you are not of this world', 'for if you were of this world, the world would love its own'. Having endured many reproaches through Christ and many dangers from when you believed, advance in enduring to the end, because 'the one having endured to the end, this one will be saved'. Know that according to Peter you will exult, 'a little now, if it is necessary, having been grieved in various trials, so that the testing of your faith, more valuable than gold perishing and tested through fire, be found to praise and glory and honour in the revelation of Jesus Christ'. But hear 'having been grieved' instead of 'having toiled', as is clear also from 'in griefs you will bear children'; for not altogether in grief at the suffering does a woman give birth, but in toil. If indeed useful to the disciples of Christ is: 'do not love the world nor the things in the world; if anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him; because all in the world, the desire of the flesh and the desire of the eyes and the boastfulness of life, is not from the Father but from the world; and the world passes away and its desire', do not then love the things passing away, but doing the will of God become worthy of becoming one together with Son and Father and Holy Spirit according to the prayer of the Saviour saying: 'as I and you are one, that they also may be one in us'. How many days is it possible to gain, having loved 'the world' or 'the things in the world', and suffering loss of or destroying one's own soul and carrying around a conscience weighed beyond 'a heavy burden' and weighed down by the fall of the denial? Let each of us recall how often he was in danger of dying the common death, and let us reckon whether perhaps for this we were kept, so that baptized in our own blood and washed off from every sin we may make our dwelling beside the altar in heaven with those who contended together with us.
pass_b_english: By your eagerness for martyrdom give room to the Spirit of your Father, who speaks in those handed over for their godliness (Matthew 10:20). If you see yourselves hated and loathed and thought to be ungodly, then take up the words, “Because of this the world hates you,” “because you are not of this world”; “if you were of this world, the world would love its own” (John 15:19). You have borne many reproaches for Christ's sake and many dangers since you came to believe: go forward in endurance to the end, since “he who endures to the end will be saved” (Matthew 10:22). Know that, as Peter says, you will rejoice, “though now for a little while, if need be, you have been grieved by various trials, so that the proof of your faith, more precious than gold that perishes though it is tested by fire, may be found to praise and glory and honour at the revelation of Jesus Christ” (1 Peter 1:6-7). But hear “grieved” in the sense of “having laboured”, as is clear also from “In grief you will bear children” (Genesis 3:16); for a woman does not always give birth in grief at what she suffers, but in labour.

If the saying is useful to Christ's disciples, “Do not love the world or the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him. For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh and the lust of the eyes and the pride of life, is not of the Father but is of the world. And the world is passing away, and its lust” (1 John 2:15-17), then do not love the things that pass away. Do the will of God and become worthy to be one with the Son and the Father and the Holy Spirit, according to the Saviour's prayer, when he says, “As I and you are one, that they also may be one in us” (John 17:21-22). And how many days can a man gain by loving “the world” or “the things in the world” while he loses or destroys his own soul and carries about a conscience weighed down beyond “a heavy burden” (Psalm 38:4), weighed down by the fall of denial? Let each of us remember how often he has been in danger of dying the common death, and let us consider whether we may not have been kept for this: that, baptized in our own blood and washed of every sin, we may pass our days beside the altar in heaven with those who have contended alongside us.
